title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 347 (Disposal of books and papers of company)

content.overview: When the affairs of a company have been completely wound up and it is about to be dissolved, the books and papers of the company and those of the Company Liquidator may be disposed of in such manner as the Tribunal directs.
content.glance: On complete winding up and impending dissolution, books and papers of the company and Liquidator are disposed of as the Tribunal directs.
content.study: Section 347 governs the fate of records at the end of the process. When the affairs of the company have been completely wound up and it is about to be dissolved, the books and papers of the company and of the Company Liquidator may be disposed of in such manner as the Tribunal directs. (IBC amended the text to centre Tribunal direction in place of earlier dual routes.) The provision prevents indefinite retention while ensuring controlled disposal under judicial oversight.

sections.heading: Disposal on completion
sections.body: When affairs are completely wound up and dissolution is imminent, books and papers of the company and Liquidator are disposed of as the Tribunal directs.

provisions.title: Disposal of books and papers of company

examples.title: Tribunal direction for destruction
examples.body: After final accounts and dissolution order, the Tribunal directs under s. 347 that the Liquidator may destroy the company’s books after retaining electronic copies for a specified period.

hypotheticals.question: May the Liquidator destroy books of his own motion at the end of the winding up?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Disposal is in such manner as the Tribunal directs under s. 347.
